name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_KINETICTHEORY_STATEMENT_Q04 - Maxwell speed distribution and temperature dependence

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: In the Maxwell-Boltzmann molecular speed distribution for an ideal gas, the most probable speed \(v_{\mathrm{mp}}\) is greater than the root-mean-square speed \(v_{\mathrm{rms}}\).

Statement II: When the absolute temperature of an ideal gas is quadrupled, the root-mean-square speed of its molecules increases by a factor of four.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: किसी आदर्श गैस के लिए मैक्सवेल-बोल्ट्ज़मान आण्विक चाल वितरण में, सर्वाधिक प्रसंभाव्य चाल \(v_{\mathrm{mp}}\) का मान वर्ग-माध्य-मूल चाल \(v_{\mathrm{rms}}\) से अधिक होता है।

कथन II: जब किसी आदर्श गैस का परम ताप चार गुना कर दिया जाता है, तो उसके अणुओं की वर्ग-माध्य-मूल चाल चार गुना बढ़ जाती है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Formulae for Characteristic Speeds in Maxwellian Distribution
In the Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution of molecular speeds, the characteristic speeds for a gas of molar mass \(M\) at absolute temperature \(T\) are: \[v_{\mathrm{mp}} = \sqrt{\frac{2RT}{M}} \approx 1.414\sqrt{\frac{RT}{M}}\] \[\overline{v} = \sqrt{\frac{8RT}{\pi M}} \approx 1.596\sqrt{\frac{RT}{M}}\] \[v_{\mathrm{rms}} = \sqrt{\frac{3RT}{M}} \approx 1.732\sqrt{\frac{RT}{M}}\] Comparing these coefficients shows the strict ordering: \[v_{\mathrm{mp}} < \overline{v} < v_{\mathrm{rms}}\]

Step 2: Evaluation of the Assertion Comparing Characteristic Speeds
The proposition asserting that \(v_{\mathrm{mp}}\) exceeds \(v_{\mathrm{rms}}\) is incorrect, because the root-mean-square speed is demonstrably greater than the most probable speed (\(1.732 > 1.414\)).

Step 3: Evaluation of the Assertion on Temperature Scaling of Speed
The root-mean-square speed is proportional to the square root of the absolute temperature: \[v_{\mathrm{rms}} \propto \sqrt{T}\] If the absolute temperature is increased by a factor of 4 (\(T' = 4T\)), the new root-mean-square speed becomes: \[v_{\mathrm{rms}}' = \sqrt{\frac{3R(4T)}{M}} = 2\sqrt{\frac{3RT}{M}} = 2 v_{\mathrm{rms}}\] Thus, quadrupling the temperature doubles the root-mean-square speed; it does not quadruple it.

Step 4: Conclusion
Both stated propositions are factually and mathematically incorrect.

Final Answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.

चरण 1: मैक्सवेल चाल वितरण में अभिलाक्षणिक चालों के सूत्र
परम ताप \(T\) और मोलर द्रव्यमान \(M\) पर मैक्सवेल-बोल्ट्ज़मान चाल वितरण में अभिलाक्षणिक चालें निम्नलिखित हैं: \[v_{\mathrm{mp}} = \sqrt{\frac{2RT}{M}} \approx 1.414\sqrt{\frac{RT}{M}}\] \[\overline{v} = \sqrt{\frac{8RT}{\pi M}} \approx 1.596\sqrt{\frac{RT}{M}}\] \[v_{\mathrm{rms}} = \sqrt{\frac{3RT}{M}} \approx 1.732\sqrt{\frac{RT}{M}}\] इन मानों की तुलना से स्पष्ट क्रम प्राप्त होता है: \[v_{\mathrm{mp}} < \overline{v} < v_{\mathrm{rms}}\]

चरण 2: अभिलाक्षणिक चालों की तुलना संबंधी दावे का मूल्यांकन
यह दावा कि \(v_{\mathrm{mp}}\) का मान \(v_{\mathrm{rms}}\) से अधिक होता है, गलत है क्योंकि वर्ग-माध्य-मूल चाल सर्वाधिक प्रसंभाव्य चाल से बड़ी होती है (\(1.732 > 1.414\))।

चरण 3: ताप पर चाल की निर्भरता संबंधी दावे का मूल्यांकन
वर्ग-माध्य-मूल चाल परम ताप के वर्गमूल के समानुपाती होती है: \[v_{\mathrm{rms}} \propto \sqrt{T}\] यदि परम ताप को 4 गुना कर दिया जाए (\(T' = 4T\)), तो नई वर्ग-माध्य-मूल चाल होगी: \[v_{\mathrm{rms}}' = \sqrt{\frac{3R(4T)}{M}} = 2\sqrt{\frac{3RT}{M}} = 2 v_{\mathrm{rms}}\] अतः, परम ताप को चार गुना करने पर वर्ग-माध्य-मूल चाल 2 गुना होती है, 4 गुना नहीं।

चरण 4: निष्कर्ष
दोनों दिए गए कथन गलत हैं।

अंतिम उत्तर: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_KINETICTHEORY_STATEMENT_Q05 - Equipartition theorem and molecular vibrational degrees

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: According to the law of equipartition of energy, each translational and rotational degree of freedom of a gas molecule contributes an average energy of \(\frac{1}{2}k_{\mathrm{B}}T\) in thermal equilibrium.

Statement II: Each vibrational mode of a diatomic molecule contributes an average energy of \(\frac{1}{2}k_{\mathrm{B}}T\) because its vibrational potential energy term is zero.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: ऊर्जा के समविभाजन नियम के अनुसार, ऊष्मीय साम्यावस्था में किसी गैस अणु की प्रत्येक स्थानांतरीय और घूर्णी स्वातंत्र्य कोटि \(\frac{1}{2}k_{\mathrm{B}}T\) की औसत ऊर्जा का योगदान देती है।

कथन II: एक द्विपरमाणुक अणु की प्रत्येक कंपन विधा \(\frac{1}{2}k_{\mathrm{B}}T\) की औसत ऊर्जा का योगदान करती है क्योंकि इसकी कंपन स्थितिज ऊर्जा का पद शून्य होता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: The Principle of Equipartition of Energy
The law of equipartition of energy states that in thermal equilibrium at temperature \(T\), the total energy of a dynamical system is equally distributed among its independent quadratic degrees of freedom, and each quadratic term in the coordinate or momentum contributes an average energy of \(\frac{1}{2}k_{\mathrm{B}}T\). Translational kinetic energy terms (\(\frac{1}{2}mv_x^2\), \(\frac{1}{2}mv_y^2\), \(\frac{1}{2}mv_z^2\)) and rotational kinetic energy terms (\(\frac{1}{2}I_1\omega_1^2\), \(\frac{1}{2}I_2\omega_2^2\)) are single quadratic terms; hence each contributes \(\frac{1}{2}k_{\mathrm{B}}T\).

Step 2: Evaluation of the Assertion on Translational and Rotational Degrees
The proposition asserting that every translational and rotational degree of freedom contributes \(\frac{1}{2}k_{\mathrm{B}}T\) to the average energy per molecule is scientifically precise and correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Assertion on Vibrational Modes
A vibrational mode in a molecule involves both kinetic energy of oscillation and elastic potential energy: \[E_{\mathrm{vib}} = \frac{1}{2}m\left(\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t}\right)^2 + \frac{1}{2}k y^2\] Because there are two independent quadratic terms (one kinetic and one potential), each vibrational mode contributes: \[\overline{E}_{\mathrm{vib}} = \frac{1}{2}k_{\mathrm{B}}T + \frac{1}{2}k_{\mathrm{B}}T = k_{\mathrm{B}}T\] The assertion that vibrational potential energy is zero and that a vibrational mode contributes only \(\frac{1}{2}k_{\mathrm{B}}T\) is therefore false.

Step 4: Conclusion
The first statement is correct, while the second statement is incorrect.

Final Answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

चरण 1: ऊर्जा समविभाजन का सिद्धांत
ऊर्जा समविभाजन नियम के अनुसार, ताप \(T\) पर ऊष्मीय साम्यावस्था में किसी गतिक निकाय की कुल ऊर्जा उसकी स्वतंत्र द्विघाती स्वातंत्र्य कोटियों में समान रूप से विभाजित होती है, तथा स्थिति या संवेग का प्रत्येक द्विघाती पद औसतन \(\frac{1}{2}k_{\mathrm{B}}T\) ऊर्जा का योगदान देता है। स्थानांतरीय गतिज ऊर्जा पद (\(\frac{1}{2}mv_x^2\), आदि) और घूर्णी गतिज ऊर्जा पद (\(\frac{1}{2}I\omega^2\), आदि) एकल द्विघाती पद होते हैं, अतः प्रत्येक \(\frac{1}{2}k_{\mathrm{B}}T\) का योगदान देता है।

चरण 2: स्थानांतरीय और घूर्णी कोटियों संबंधी दावे का मूल्यांकन
यह दावा कि प्रत्येक स्थानांतरीय और घूर्णी स्वातंत्र्य कोटि प्रति अणु \(\frac{1}{2}k_{\mathrm{B}}T\) ऊर्जा का योगदान देती है, पूर्णतः सटीक और सही है।

चरण 3: कंपन विधा संबंधी दावे का मूल्यांकन
अणु में एक कंपन विधा में दोलन की गतिज ऊर्जा और प्रत्यास्थ स्थितिज ऊर्जा दोनों सम्मिलित होती हैं: \[E_{\mathrm{vib}} = \frac{1}{2}m\left(\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t}\right)^2 + \frac{1}{2}k y^2\] चूँकि इसमें दो स्वतंत्र द्विघाती पद (एक गतिज तथा एक स्थितिज) होते हैं, अतः प्रत्येक कंपन विधा निम्नलिखित ऊर्जा प्रदान करती है: \[\overline{E}_{\mathrm{vib}} = \frac{1}{2}k_{\mathrm{B}}T + \frac{1}{2}k_{\mathrm{B}}T = k_{\mathrm{B}}T\] अतः यह दावा कि स्थितिज ऊर्जा शून्य होती है और कंपन विधा केवल \(\frac{1}{2}k_{\mathrm{B}}T\) का योगदान देती है, गलत है।

चरण 4: निष्कर्ष
प्रथम कथन सही है, जबकि द्वितीय कथन गलत है।

अंतिम उत्तर: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_KINETICTHEORY_STATEMENT_Q06 - Molar heat capacities of diatomic gas

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: For a rigid diatomic gas molecule without active vibrational modes, the molar heat capacity at constant volume is \(C_V = \frac{5}{2}R\).

Statement II: The ratio of specific heats \(\gamma = \frac{C_P}{C_V}\) for an ideal rigid diatomic gas is equal to \(\frac{7}{5} = 1.40\).

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: सक्रिय कंपन विधाओं से रहित एक दृढ़ द्विपरमाणुक गैस के लिए, नियत आयतन पर मोलर ऊष्मा धारिता \(C_V = \frac{5}{2}R\) होती है।

कथन II: एक आदर्श दृढ़ द्विपरमाणुक गैस के लिए विशिष्ट ऊष्माओं का अनुपात \(\gamma = \frac{C_P}{C_V}\), \(\frac{7}{5} = 1.40\) के बराबर होता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Degrees of Freedom of a Rigid Diatomic Gas
A diatomic molecule modeled as a rigid rotator has 3 translational degrees of freedom and 2 rotational degrees of freedom (rotation about the internuclear axis has negligible moment of inertia and is inactive). Thus, the total number of degrees of freedom is \(f = 3 + 2 = 5\).

Step 2: Derivation and Evaluation of Molar Heat Capacity at Constant Volume
By the equipartition theorem, the internal energy of one mole of a rigid diatomic gas is: \[U = N_{\mathrm{A}} \times 5 \times \left(\frac{1}{2}k_{\mathrm{B}}T\right) = \frac{5}{2}RT\] The molar heat capacity at constant volume is the temperature derivative of internal energy: \[C_V = \frac{\mathrm{d}U}{\mathrm{d}T} = \frac{5}{2}R\] The assertion that \(C_V = \frac{5}{2}R\) is therefore completely correct.

Step 3: Derivation and Evaluation of Specific Heat Ratio
Using Mayer's relation for an ideal gas, \(C_P - C_V = R\): \[C_P = C_V + R = \frac{5}{2}R + R = \frac{7}{2}R\] The adiabatic ratio \(\gamma\) is the quotient of the two molar heat capacities: \[\gamma = \frac{C_P}{C_V} = \frac{\frac{7}{2}R}{\frac{5}{2}R} = \frac{7}{5} = 1.40\] The assertion that \(\gamma = \frac{7}{5} = 1.40\) is therefore completely correct.

Step 4: Conclusion
Both stated propositions are physically sound and correct.

Final Answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

चरण 1: दृढ़ द्विपरमाणुक गैस की स्वातंत्र्य कोटियाँ
एक दृढ़ घूर्णी द्विपरमाणुक अणु में 3 स्थानांतरीय स्वातंत्र्य कोटियाँ तथा 2 घूर्णी स्वातंत्र्य कोटियाँ होती हैं (अंतर-नाभिकीय अक्ष के परितः जड़त्व आघूर्ण नगण्य होने के कारण घूर्णन निष्क्रिय रहता है)। अतः कुल स्वातंत्र्य कोटियाँ \(f = 3 + 2 = 5\) होती हैं।

चरण 2: नियत आयतन पर मोलर ऊष्मा धारिता की व्युत्पत्ति एवं मूल्यांकन
ऊर्जा समविभाजन नियम के अनुसार, एक मोल दृढ़ द्विपरमाणुक गैस की आंतरिक ऊर्जा है: \[U = N_{\mathrm{A}} \times 5 \times \left(\frac{1}{2}k_{\mathrm{B}}T\right) = \frac{5}{2}RT\] नियत आयतन पर मोलर ऊष्मा धारिता आंतरिक ऊर्जा का ताप के सापेक्ष अवकलन है: \[C_V = \frac{\mathrm{d}U}{\mathrm{d}T} = \frac{5}{2}R\] अतः \(C_V = \frac{5}{2}R\) होने का दावा पूर्णतः सत्य है।

चरण 3: विशिष्ट ऊष्मा अनुपात की व्युत्पत्ति एवं मूल्यांकन
आदर्श गैस के लिए मेयर संबंध \(C_P - C_V = R\) का उपयोग करने पर: \[C_P = C_V + R = \frac{5}{2}R + R = \frac{7}{2}R\] विशिष्ट ऊष्माओं का अनुपात \(\gamma\) दोनों मोलर ऊष्मा धारिताओं का भागफल होता है: \[\gamma = \frac{C_P}{C_V} = \frac{\frac{7}{2}R}{\frac{5}{2}R} = \frac{7}{5} = 1.40\] अतः \(\gamma = \frac{7}{5} = 1.40\) होने का दावा भी पूर्णतः सत्य है।

चरण 4: निष्कर्ष
दिए गए दोनों कथन भौतिक रूप से पूर्णतः सही हैं।

अंतिम उत्तर: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_KINETICTHEORY_STATEMENT_Q07 - Mean free path pressure and diameter

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: At a constant temperature, doubling the pressure of an ideal gas doubles the mean free path of its molecules.

Statement II: The mean free path of ideal gas molecules is inversely proportional to the square of their molecular diameter.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: नियत ताप पर, किसी आदर्श गैस का दाब दोगुना करने पर उसके अणुओं का माध्य मुक्त पथ दोगुना हो जाता है।

कथन II: आदर्श गैस अणुओं का माध्य मुक्त पथ उनके आण्विक व्यास के वर्ग के व्युत्क्रमानुपाती होता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Governing Formula for Mean Free Path
The mean free path \(l\) of a gas molecule of effective diameter \(d\) moving in a gas with number density \(n\) is given by: \[l = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2} n \pi d^2}\] Using the ideal gas equation of state in terms of number density, \(P = n k_{\mathrm{B}} T\), the number density is \(n = \frac{P}{k_{\mathrm{B}} T}\). Substituting this into the mean free path expression yields: \[l = \frac{k_{\mathrm{B}} T}{\sqrt{2} \pi d^2 P}\]

Step 2: Evaluation of the Assertion on Pressure Dependence
At a constant absolute temperature \(T\), the mean free path is inversely proportional to pressure: \[l \propto \frac{1}{P}\] When the pressure is doubled (\(P' = 2P\)), the new mean free path becomes: \[l' = \frac{l}{2}\] Doubling the pressure halves the mean free path rather than doubling it. Therefore, the assertion claiming that the mean free path doubles is incorrect.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Assertion on Molecular Diameter Dependence
From the formula \(l = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2} n \pi d^2}\), the collision cross-section is \(\sigma = \pi d^2\). Because the target area swept out by a molecule is proportional to the square of its diameter, the mean free path is strictly inversely proportional to \(d^2\) (\(l \propto \frac{1}{d^2}\)). Thus, this assertion is entirely correct.

Step 4: Conclusion
The first statement is incorrect, whereas the second statement is correct.

Final Answer: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

चरण 1: माध्य मुक्त पथ का मूल सूत्र
संख्या घनत्व \(n\) वाली गैस में प्रभावी आण्विक व्यास \(d\) वाले अणु का माध्य मुक्त पथ \(l\) निम्नलिखित सूत्र द्वारा दिया जाता है: \[l = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2} n \pi d^2}\] संख्या घनत्व के पदों में आदर्श गैस समीकरण \(P = n k_{\mathrm{B}} T\) से, \(n = \frac{P}{k_{\mathrm{B}} T}\) प्राप्त होता है। इसे माध्य मुक्त पथ के सूत्र में रखने पर: \[l = \frac{k_{\mathrm{B}} T}{\sqrt{2} \pi d^2 P}\]

चरण 2: दाब निर्भरता संबंधी दावे का मूल्यांकन
नियत परम ताप \(T\) पर, माध्य मुक्त पथ दाब के व्युत्क्रमानुपाती होता है: \[l \propto \frac{1}{P}\] जब दाब को दोगुना (\(P' = 2P\)) किया जाता है, तो नया माध्य मुक्त पथ होगा: \[l' = \frac{l}{2}\] दाब दोगुना करने पर माध्य मुक्त पथ आधा हो जाता है, दोगुना नहीं। अतः माध्य मुक्त पथ दोगुना होने का दावा गलत है।

चरण 3: आण्विक व्यास पर निर्भरता संबंधी दावे का मूल्यांकन
सूत्र \(l = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2} n \pi d^2}\) से, संघट्ट परिच्छेद क्षेत्रफल \(\sigma = \pi d^2\) होता है। चूँकि अणु द्वारा तय किया गया प्रभावी क्षेत्रफल व्यास के वर्ग के समानुपाती होता है, इसलिए माध्य मुक्त पथ निश्चित रूप से \(d^2\) के व्युत्क्रमानुपाती होता है (\(l \propto \frac{1}{d^2}\))। अतः यह दावा पूर्णतः सही है।

चरण 4: निष्कर्ष
प्रथम कथन गलत है, जबकि द्वितीय कथन सही है।

अंतिम उत्तर: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_KINETICTHEORY_STATEMENT_Q08 - Dulong Petit law and real gas

questiontext.text:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: According to the Dulong-Petit law, the molar heat capacity of diamond at room temperature is equal to \(3R \approx 25\text{ J mol}^{-1}\text{ K}^{-1}\).

Statement II: Real gases behave most like an ideal gas at very low temperatures and very high pressures because intermolecular interactions become negligible.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

नीचे दो कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: ड्यूलोंग-पेटिट नियम के अनुसार, कमरे के ताप पर हीरे की मोलर ऊष्मा धारिता \(3R \approx 25\text{ J mol}^{-1}\text{ K}^{-1}\) के बराबर होती है।

कथन II: वास्तविक गैसें अत्यधिक निम्न ताप और अत्यधिक उच्च दाब पर आदर्श गैस के समान व्यवहार करती हैं क्योंकि अंतराआण्विक अन्योन्यक्रियाएं नगण्य हो जाती हैं।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सबसे उपयुक्त उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Dulong-Petit Law for Diamond
The classical Dulong-Petit law predicts that the molar heat capacity of solid elements is \(C = 3R \approx 24.9\text{ J mol}^{-1}\text{ K}^{-1}\) at sufficiently high temperatures where all three-dimensional vibrational oscillator modes are fully active. However, for diamond (carbon), the carbon-carbon covalent bonds are exceptionally strong and the atoms have small mass, resulting in extremely high vibrational frequencies. Consequently, at room temperature (\(\sim 300\text{ K}\)), quantum effects freeze out most vibrational modes, and the molar heat capacity of diamond is only about \(6.1\text{ J mol}^{-1}\text{ K}^{-1}\), which is far below \(3R\). Therefore, the claim that diamond reaches \(3R\) at room temperature is false.

Step 2: Physical Conditions for Real Gas Ideality
An ideal gas assumes point-mass particles with zero finite volume and no intermolecular attractive or repulsive forces. For real gases, intermolecular forces become negligible only when molecules possess large kinetic energies (high temperature) and are spaced far apart (low pressure and low density). Conversely, at very low temperatures, molecular kinetic energy is small compared to attractive potential energy, and at very high pressures, molecules are forced close together so their finite volume cannot be neglected. Hence, real gases deviate maximally from ideality at low temperatures and high pressures, and approach ideality at high temperatures and low pressures.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Assertion on Real Gas Behavior
The proposition asserting that real gases behave ideally at very low temperatures and very high pressures contradicts fundamental kinetic theory and is incorrect.

Step 4: Conclusion
Both stated propositions are scientifically inaccurate and incorrect.

Final Answer: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.

चरण 1: हीरे के लिए ड्यूलोंग-पेटिट नियम का मूल्यांकन
चिरसम्मत ड्यूलोंग-पेटिट नियम यह भविष्यवाणी करता है कि पर्याप्त उच्च ताप पर ठोस तत्वों की मोलर ऊष्मा धारिता \(C = 3R \approx 24.9\text{ J mol}^{-1}\text{ K}^{-1}\) होती है, जहाँ सभी त्रिविमीय दोलित्र विधाएं पूर्णतः सक्रिय हो जाती हैं। किंतु हीरे (कार्बन) में कार्बन-कार्बन सहसंयोजक बंध अत्यधिक प्रबल होते हैं और परमाणुओं का द्रव्यमान कम होता है, जिससे इनकी कंपन आवृत्तियां बहुत उच्च होती हैं। परिणामस्वरूप, कमरे के ताप (\(\sim 300\text{ K}\)) पर क्वांटम प्रभावों के कारण अधिकांश कंपन विधाएं प्रसुप्त (frozen out) रहती हैं, और हीरे की मोलर ऊष्मा धारिता केवल लगभग \(6.1\text{ J mol}^{-1}\text{ K}^{-1}\) होती है, जो \(3R\) से बहुत कम है। अतः यह दावा कि कमरे के ताप पर हीरे की ऊष्मा धारिता \(3R\) होती है, गलत है।

चरण 2: वास्तविक गैसों के आदर्श व्यवहार की भौतिक परिस्थितियां
आदर्श गैस मॉडल में कणों का आयतन शून्य तथा अंतराआण्विक बल नगण्य माने जाते हैं। वास्तविक गैसों में अंतराआण्विक बल केवल तभी नगण्य होते हैं जब अणुओं की गतिज ऊर्जा बहुत अधिक हो (उच्च ताप) और वे एक दूसरे से काफी दूर हों (निम्न दाब एवं निम्न घनत्व)। इसके विपरीत, अत्यंत निम्न ताप पर गतिज ऊर्जा कम होने से आकर्षण बल प्रभावी हो जाते हैं तथा अत्यधिक उच्च दाब पर अणुओं का परिमित आयतन उपेक्षणीय नहीं रहता। अतः वास्तविक गैसें उच्च ताप और निम्न दाब पर आदर्श व्यवहार दर्शाती हैं, न कि निम्न ताप और उच्च दाब पर।

चरण 3: वास्तविक गैस व्यवहार संबंधी दावे का मूल्यांकन
यह दावा कि वास्तविक गैसें अत्यधिक निम्न ताप और उच्च दाब पर आदर्श गैस के समान व्यवहार करती हैं, अणुगति सिद्धांत के विपरीत और गलत है।

चरण 4: निष्कर्ष
दिए गए दोनों कथन असत्य और गलत हैं।

अंतिम उत्तर: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.

answer.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_KINETICTHEORY_STATEMENT_Q01 - Avogadro hypothesis and Dalton partial pressure

questiontext.text:
Given below are three statements:

Statement I: Avogadro's hypothesis states that equal volumes of all gases under identical conditions of temperature and pressure contain equal numbers of molecules.

Statement II: Dalton's law of partial pressures states that the total pressure exerted by a mixture of non-reactive ideal gases is equal to the sum of the partial pressures of individual gases.

Statement III: The universal gas constant \(R\) varies depending on the nature and chemical composition of the ideal gas.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

नीचे तीन कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: आवोगाद्रो की परिकल्पना के अनुसार, समान ताप और दाब की परिस्थितियों में सभी गैसों के समान आयतन में अणुओं की संख्या समान होती है।

कथन II: डाल्टन के आंशिक दाब के नियमानुसार, परस्पर अक्रियाशील आदर्श गैसों के मिश्रण द्वारा लगाया गया कुल दाब, घटक गैसों के आंशिक दाबों के योग के बराबर होता है।

कथन III: सार्वत्रिक गैस नियतांक \(R\) का मान आदर्श गैस की प्रकृति और उसके रासायनिक संघटन पर निर्भर करता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the First Proposition Regarding Avogadro's Hypothesis
Avogadro's hypothesis states that equal volumes of all gases at the same temperature and pressure contain the same number of molecules. From the ideal gas law \(PV = N k_{\mathrm{B}} T\), if pressure \(P\), volume \(V\), and temperature \(T\) are identical, the total number of molecules \(N = \frac{PV}{k_{\mathrm{B}}T}\) is strictly identical for any gas. Therefore, the first proposition is scientifically accurate and correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Second Proposition Regarding Dalton's Law
For a mixture of non-reactive ideal gases confined within a vessel of volume \(V\) at absolute temperature \(T\), each gas component behaves independently. The total pressure is given by \(P = \sum_{i} P_i = \sum_{i} \frac{\mu_i R T}{V}\), where \(P_i\) represents the partial pressure of component \(i\). Hence, the total pressure of a mixture of non-interacting ideal gases is the sum of the individual partial pressures. Therefore, the second proposition is scientifically accurate and correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Third Proposition Regarding the Universal Gas Constant
The universal gas constant \(R = N_{\mathrm{A}} k_{\mathrm{B}} \approx 8.314\text{ J mol}^{-1}\text{ K}^{-1}\) is a fundamental physical constant. It has the exact same value for all ideal gases, irrespective of their molecular mass, chemical formula, or atomicity. Therefore, the proposition claiming that \(R\) varies with the nature of the gas is incorrect.

Step 4: Conclusion
Only the first and second propositions are correct, while the third proposition is incorrect.

Final Answer: Statements I and II only

चरण 1: आवोगाद्रो की परिकल्पना संबंधी प्रथम कथन का मूल्यांकन
आवोगाद्रो की परिकल्पना के अनुसार, समान ताप और दाब पर सभी गैसों के समान आयतन में अणुओं की संख्या समान होती है। आदर्श गैस समीकरण \(PV = N k_{\mathrm{B}} T\) से, यदि दाब \(P\), आयतन \(V\) और ताप \(T\) समान हों, तो कुल अणुओं की संख्या \(N = \frac{PV}{k_{\mathrm{B}}T}\) प्रत्येक गैस के लिए निश्चित रूप से समान होगी। अतः प्रथम कथन वैज्ञानिक रूप से पूर्णतः सही है।

चरण 2: डाल्टन के नियम संबंधी द्वितीय कथन का मूल्यांकन
परम ताप \(T\) पर \(V\) आयतन के पात्र में उपस्थित परस्पर अक्रियाशील आदर्श गैसों के मिश्रण में प्रत्येक घटक गैस स्वतंत्र रूप से व्यवहार करती है। कुल दाब \(P = \sum_{i} P_i = \sum_{i} \frac{\mu_i R T}{V}\) होता है, जहाँ \(P_i\) घटक \(i\) का आंशिक दाब है। अतः आदर्श गैसों के मिश्रण का कुल दाब व्यक्तिगत आंशिक दाबों के योग के बराबर होता है। अतः द्वितीय कथन वैज्ञानिक रूप से पूर्णतः सही है।

चरण 3: सार्वत्रिक गैस नियतांक संबंधी तृतीय कथन का मूल्यांकन
सार्वत्रिक गैस नियतांक \(R = N_{\mathrm{A}} k_{\mathrm{B}} \approx 8.314\text{ J mol}^{-1}\text{ K}^{-1}\) एक मूलभूत भौतिक नियतांक है। इसका मान सभी आदर्श गैसों के लिए समान होता है, चाहे उनका आण्विक द्रव्यमान, रासायनिक सूत्र या परमाणुकता कुछ भी हो। अतः यह दावा कि \(R\) गैस की प्रकृति पर निर्भर करता है, गलत है।

चरण 4: निष्कर्ष
केवल प्रथम और द्वितीय कथन सही हैं, जबकि तृतीय कथन गलत है।

अंतिम उत्तर: Statements I and II only

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_KINETICTHEORY_STATEMENT_Q02 - Kinetic wall collisions and root mean square speed

questiontext.text:
Given below are three statements:

Statement I: The pressure exerted by an ideal gas on the container walls is caused by completely inelastic collisions between the gas molecules and the walls.

Statement II: The root-mean-square speed of ideal gas molecules is inversely proportional to the square root of the molar mass of the gas at a fixed temperature.

Statement III: At the same temperature, lighter gas molecules have a greater root-mean-square speed than heavier gas molecules.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

नीचे तीन कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: पात्र की दीवारों पर आदर्श गैस द्वारा लगाया गया दाब, गैस अणुओं और दीवारों के बीच होने वाले पूर्णतः अप्रत्यास्थ संघट्टों के कारण उत्पन्न होता है।

कथन II: एक निश्चित ताप पर आदर्श गैस के अणुओं की वर्ग-माध्य-मूल चाल, गैस के मोलर द्रव्यमान के वर्गमूल के व्युत्क्रमानुपाती होती है।

कथन III: समान ताप पर, हल्के गैस अणुओं की वर्ग-माध्य-मूल चाल भारी गैस अणुओं की तुलना में अधिक होती है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of the First Proposition Regarding Wall Collisions
In the kinetic theory of gases, molecules are assumed to undergo perfectly elastic collisions with the walls of the container. During each elastic collision of a molecule of mass \(m\) moving with velocity component \(v_x\) perpendicular to a wall, the momentum transferred to the wall is \(2mv_x\), and mechanical kinetic energy is conserved. Inelastic collisions would result in continuous energy loss and temperature drop. Therefore, the assertion that wall collisions are completely inelastic is incorrect.

Step 2: Evaluation of the Second Proposition Regarding Root-Mean-Square Speed Formula
From kinetic theory, the root-mean-square speed of ideal gas molecules is given by: \[v_{\mathrm{rms}} = \sqrt{\frac{3k_{\mathrm{B}}T}{m}} = \sqrt{\frac{3RT}{M}}\] At a constant absolute temperature \(T\), the factor \(\sqrt{3RT}\) is constant, which directly implies: \[v_{\mathrm{rms}} \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{M}}\] Thus, the root-mean-square speed is strictly inversely proportional to the square root of the molar mass. Therefore, the second proposition is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of the Third Proposition Comparing Speeds of Lighter and Heavier Molecules
Because \(v_{\mathrm{rms}} \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{M}}\) at equal temperatures, a gas with a smaller molar mass \(M\) will have a larger root-mean-square speed than a gas with a larger molar mass. For instance, at \(300\text{ K}\), helium (\(M = 4\text{ g mol}^{-1}\)) has a significantly larger root-mean-square speed than argon (\(M \approx 40\text{ g mol}^{-1}\)). Therefore, the third proposition is correct.

Step 4: Conclusion
The first proposition is incorrect, while the second and third propositions are correct.

Final Answer: Statements II and III only

चरण 1: दीवारों से संघट्ट संबंधी प्रथम कथन का मूल्यांकन
गैस अणुगति सिद्धांत में यह माना जाता है कि गैस के अणु पात्र की दीवारों से पूर्णतः प्रत्यास्थ संघट्ट करते हैं। दीवार के लंबवत \(v_x\) वेग घटक से गतिशील द्रव्यमान \(m\) के अणु द्वारा प्रत्यास्थ संघट्ट में दीवार को स्थानांतरित संवेग \(2mv_x\) होता है तथा यांत्रिक गतिज ऊर्जा संरक्षित रहती है। यदि संघट्ट अप्रत्यास्थ होते, तो निरंतर ऊर्जा ह्रास और ताप में गिरावट होती। अतः संघट्ट को पूर्णतः अप्रत्यास्थ बताने वाला प्रथम कथन गलत है।

चरण 2: वर्ग-माध्य-मूल चाल सूत्र संबंधी द्वितीय कथन का मूल्यांकन
अणुगति सिद्धांत के अनुसार आदर्श गैस अणुओं की वर्ग-माध्य-मूल चाल का सूत्र है: \[v_{\mathrm{rms}} = \sqrt{\frac{3k_{\mathrm{B}}T}{m}} = \sqrt{\frac{3RT}{M}}\] नियत परम ताप \(T\) पर, पद \(\sqrt{3RT}\) नियत रहता है, जिससे प्राप्त होता है: \[v_{\mathrm{rms}} \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{M}}\] अतः वर्ग-माध्य-मूल चाल मोलर द्रव्यमान के वर्गमूल के व्युत्क्रमानुपाती होती है। अतः द्वितीय कथन सही है।

चरण 3: हल्के व भारी अणुओं की चाल तुलना संबंधी तृतीय कथन का मूल्यांकन
समान ताप पर \(v_{\mathrm{rms}} \propto \frac{1}{\sqrt{M}}\) होने के कारण, जिस गैस का मोलर द्रव्यमान \(M\) कम होता है, उसकी वर्ग-माध्य-मूल चाल अधिक मोलर द्रव्यमान वाली गैस की तुलना में अधिक होती है। उदाहरणार्थ, \(300\text{ K}\) पर हीलियम (\(M = 4\text{ g mol}^{-1}\)) की चाल आर्गन (\(M \approx 40\text{ g mol}^{-1}\)) से काफी अधिक होती है। अतः तृतीय कथन सही है।

चरण 4: निष्कर्ष
प्रथम कथन गलत है, जबकि द्वितीय और तृतीय कथन सही हैं।

अंतिम उत्तर: Statements II and III only

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_KINETICTHEORY_STATEMENT_Q03 - Equipartition theorem and gas heat capacities

questiontext.text:
Given below are three statements:

Statement I: A monatomic ideal gas molecule possesses three degrees of freedom, all of which correspond to translational motion.

Statement II: For an ideal rigid diatomic gas with no vibrational modes, the molar heat capacity at constant volume is \(C_V = \frac{5}{2}R\).

Statement III: Each vibrational mode in a molecule contributes \(k_{\mathrm{B}}T\) to the average energy per molecule because it contains two independent quadratic terms.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

नीचे तीन कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: एकपरमाणुक आदर्श गैस के अणु में तीन स्वातंत्र्य कोटियाँ होती हैं, और ये सभी स्थानांतरीय गति से संबंधित होती हैं।

कथन II: कंपन विधाओं से रहित एक आदर्श दृढ़ द्विपरमाणुक गैस के लिए, नियत आयतन पर मोलर ऊष्मा धारिता \(C_V = \frac{5}{2}R\) होती है।

कथन III: किसी अणु में प्रत्येक कंपन विधा प्रति अणु औसत ऊर्जा में \(k_{\mathrm{B}}T\) का योगदान करती है क्योंकि इसमें दो स्वतंत्र द्विघाती पद होते हैं।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Degrees of Freedom of a Monatomic Gas
A monatomic gas atom behaves as a point mass that can move along three mutually perpendicular spatial directions (\(x\), \(y\), and \(z\)). Its moment of inertia about its own center of mass is negligibly small, so rotational energy does not contribute classically. Thus, it has strictly 3 translational degrees of freedom, with total energy \(E = \frac{1}{2}mv_x^2 + \frac{1}{2}mv_y^2 + \frac{1}{2}mv_z^2\). Therefore, the first proposition is correct.

Step 2: Evaluation of Molar Heat Capacity for a Rigid Diatomic Gas
A rigid diatomic molecule has 3 translational degrees of freedom and 2 independent rotational degrees of freedom about axes perpendicular to the internuclear axis (rotation about the internuclear axis itself has a negligible moment of inertia). The total degrees of freedom are \(f = 3 + 2 = 5\). According to the equipartition theorem, the internal energy of one mole of this gas is: \[U = N_{\mathrm{A}} \times 5 \times \left(\frac{1}{2}k_{\mathrm{B}}T\right) = \frac{5}{2}RT\] The molar heat capacity at constant volume is: \[C_V = \frac{\mathrm{d}U}{\mathrm{d}T} = \frac{5}{2}R\] Therefore, the second proposition is correct.

Step 3: Evaluation of Energy Contribution from Vibrational Modes
A vibrational mode involves both kinetic energy of oscillation and potential energy of deformation: \[E_{\mathrm{vib}} = \frac{1}{2}m\left(\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t}\right)^2 + \frac{1}{2}ky^2\] Because there are two quadratic terms, the equipartition theorem assigns \(\frac{1}{2}k_{\mathrm{B}}T\) to each term, giving a total average contribution of: \[\overline{E}_{\mathrm{vib}} = \frac{1}{2}k_{\mathrm{B}}T + \frac{1}{2}k_{\mathrm{B}}T = k_{\mathrm{B}}T\] Therefore, the third proposition is correct.

Step 4: Conclusion
All three stated propositions are scientifically verified and correct.

Final Answer: Statements I, II and III

चरण 1: एकपरमाणुक गैस की स्वातंत्र्य कोटियों संबंधी प्रथम कथन का मूल्यांकन
एकपरमाणुक गैस का परमाणु एक बिंदु द्रव्यमान की तरह व्यवहार करता है जो तीन परस्पर लंबवत दिशाओं (\(x\), \(y\), \(z\)) में गति कर सकता है। अपने द्रव्यमान केंद्र के परितः इसका जड़त्व आघूर्ण नगण्य होता है, जिससे घूर्णी ऊर्जा का कोई योगदान नहीं होता। अतः इसमें ठीक 3 स्थानांतरीय स्वातंत्र्य कोटियाँ होती हैं। अतः प्रथम कथन पूर्णतः सही है।

चरण 2: दृढ़ द्विपरमाणुक गैस की मोलर ऊष्मा धारिता संबंधी द्वितीय कथन का मूल्यांकन
एक दृढ़ द्विपरमाणुक अणु में 3 स्थानांतरीय तथा अंतर-नाभिकीय अक्ष के लंबवत 2 घूर्णी स्वातंत्र्य कोटियाँ होती हैं, जिससे कुल स्वातंत्र्य कोटियाँ \(f = 3 + 2 = 5\) होती हैं। ऊर्जा समविभाजन नियम के अनुसार, एक मोल गैस की आंतरिक ऊर्जा है: \[U = N_{\mathrm{A}} \times 5 \times \left(\frac{1}{2}k_{\mathrm{B}}T\right) = \frac{5}{2}RT\] नियत आयतन पर मोलर ऊष्मा धारिता: \[C_V = \frac{\mathrm{d}U}{\mathrm{d}T} = \frac{5}{2}R\] अतः द्वितीय कथन पूर्णतः सही है।

चरण 3: कंपन विधाओं के ऊर्जा योगदान संबंधी तृतीय कथन का मूल्यांकन
एक कंपन विधा में दोलन की गतिज ऊर्जा तथा प्रत्यास्थ स्थितिज ऊर्जा दोनों सम्मिलित होती हैं: \[E_{\mathrm{vib}} = \frac{1}{2}m\left(\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t}\right)^2 + \frac{1}{2}ky^2\] चूँकि इसमें दो स्वतंत्र द्विघाती पद होते हैं, अतः ऊर्जा समविभाजन नियम के अनुसार प्रत्येक पद \(\frac{1}{2}k_{\mathrm{B}}T\) प्रदान करता है, जिससे कुल औसत योगदान: \[\overline{E}_{\mathrm{vib}} = \frac{1}{2}k_{\mathrm{B}}T + \frac{1}{2}k_{\mathrm{B}}T = k_{\mathrm{B}}T\] होता है। अतः तृतीय कथन भी पूर्णतः सही है।

चरण 4: निष्कर्ष
दिए गए तीनों कथन वैज्ञानिक रूप से सत्य और सही हैं।

अंतिम उत्तर: Statements I, II and III

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_KINETICTHEORY_STATEMENT_Q04 - Mean free path density and scale

questiontext.text:
Given below are three statements:

Statement I: The mean free path of ideal gas molecules is inversely proportional to the number density of the molecules.

Statement II: When an ideal gas in a rigid container of fixed volume is heated so that its absolute temperature doubles, its mean free path remains unchanged.

Statement III: For typical gases at standard temperature and pressure (STP), the mean free path is of the same order of magnitude as the molecular diameter.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

नीचे तीन कथन दिए गए हैं:

कथन I: आदर्श गैस अणुओं का माध्य मुक्त पथ, अणुओं के संख्या घनत्व के व्युत्क्रमानुपाती होता है।

कथन II: जब निश्चित आयतन के दृढ़ पात्र में बंद किसी आदर्श गैस को गर्म करके उसका परम ताप दोगुना कर दिया जाता है, तो उसका माध्य मुक्त पथ अपरिवर्तित रहता है।

कथन III: मानक ताप और दाब (STP) पर सामान्य गैसों के लिए, माध्य मुक्त पथ का परिमाण आण्विक व्यास की कोटि के बराबर होता है।

उपर्युक्त कथनों के आलोक में, नीचे दिए गए विकल्पों में से सही उत्तर चुनिए:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Formula and Density Dependence of Mean Free Path
The mean free path \(l\) of a gas molecule of effective diameter \(d\) moving in a gas of number density \(n\) is given by: \[l = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2} n \pi d^2}\] This expression demonstrates that \(l\) is inversely proportional to the number density \(n\) (\(l \propto \frac{1}{n}\)) and inversely proportional to the cross-sectional area \(\pi d^2\). Therefore, the first proposition is correct.

Step 2: Temperature Dependence at Constant Volume
In a sealed, rigid container of fixed volume \(V\) containing \(N\) molecules, the number density is \(n = \frac{N}{V}\). Because neither the volume nor the total number of molecules changes, \(n\) remains strictly constant during heating. Furthermore, the molecular diameter \(d\) is an intrinsic property that does not change with temperature. Since \(l = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2} n \pi d^2}\), the mean free path \(l\) remains strictly unchanged when the gas is heated at constant volume, even though molecular speed and collision frequency increase. Therefore, the second proposition is correct.

Step 3: Comparative Scale of Mean Free Path and Molecular Diameter
For typical gas molecules (such as \(\text{N}_2\) or \(\text{O}_2\)) at standard temperature and pressure, the molecular diameter is \(d \approx 2\text{ \AA} = 2 \times 10^{-10}\text{ m}\). The calculated mean free path under STP conditions is \(l \approx 1500\text{ \AA} = 1.5 \times 10^{-7}\text{ m} \approx 1000\,d\) to \(1500\,d\). Thus, the mean free path is approximately three orders of magnitude (a thousand times) larger than the molecular diameter, rather than being of the same order of magnitude. Therefore, the third proposition is incorrect.

Step 4: Conclusion
The first and second propositions are correct, while the third proposition is incorrect.

Final Answer: Statements I and II only

चरण 1: माध्य मुक्त पथ का सूत्र एवं घनत्व निर्भरता
संख्या घनत्व \(n\) और आण्विक व्यास \(d\) वाली गैस के लिए माध्य मुक्त पथ \(l\) का सूत्र है: \[l = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2} n \pi d^2}\] यह समीकरण दर्शाता है कि \(l\) संख्या घनत्व \(n\) के व्युत्क्रमानुपाती (\(l \propto \frac{1}{n}\)) होता है। अतः प्रथम कथन पूर्णतः सही है।

चरण 2: नियत आयतन पर ताप निर्भरता का मूल्यांकन
नियत आयतन \(V\) वाले दृढ़ पात्र में बंद \(N\) अणुओं के लिए संख्या घनत्व \(n = \frac{N}{V}\) होता है। चूँकि आयतन और कुल अणुओं की संख्या दोनों स्थिर हैं, अतः गर्म करने पर \(n\) अपरिवर्तित रहता है। साथ ही आण्विक व्यास \(d\) भी ताप पर निर्भर नहीं करता। अतः \(l = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2} n \pi d^2}\) के अनुसार, नियत आयतन पर गैस को गर्म करने पर उसका माध्य मुक्त पथ पूर्णतः अपरिवर्तित रहता है, यद्यपि अणुओं की चाल और संघट्ट आवृत्ति बढ़ जाती है। अतः द्वितीय कथन पूर्णतः सही है।

चरण 3: माध्य मुक्त पथ और आण्विक व्यास के परिमाण की तुलना
मानक ताप और दाब (STP) पर सामान्य गैस अणुओं (जैसे \(\text{N}_2\) या \(\text{O}_2\)) का आण्विक व्यास \(d \approx 2\text{ \AA} = 2 \times 10^{-10}\text{ m}\) होता है। STP पर परिकलित माध्य मुक्त पथ \(l \approx 1500\text{ \AA} = 1.5 \times 10^{-7}\text{ m}\) होता है, जो व्यास का लगभग \(1000\) से \(1500\) गुना है। अतः माध्य मुक्त पथ आण्विक व्यास की तुलना में लगभग तीन कोटि (हजार गुना) बड़ा होता है, उसी कोटि का नहीं। अतः तृतीय कथन गलत है।

चरण 4: निष्कर्ष
प्रथम और द्वितीय कथन सही हैं, जबकि तृतीय कथन गलत है।

अंतिम उत्तर: Statements I and II only

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_KINETIC_THEORY_MATCHING_Q01 - Fundamental gas laws and their defining relationships

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Gas Law) List-II (Defining Relationship)
(A) Boyle's law (I) At constant pressure, volume is directly proportional to absolute temperature (\(V \propto T\))
(B) Charles' law (II) When gases combine chemically, their reacting volumes are in the ratios of small integers
(C) Gay Lussac's law (III) At constant temperature, pressure varies inversely with volume (\(P \propto \frac{1}{V}\))
(D) Avogadro's law (IV) Equal volumes of all gases at the same temperature and pressure contain equal numbers of molecules

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of Boyle's law
Boyle's law states that for a fixed mass of gas at constant temperature, the volume of the gas is inversely proportional to its pressure, or \(PV = \text{constant}\). Expressed alternatively, pressure varies inversely with volume (\(P \propto \frac{1}{V}\)). Therefore, Boyle's law corresponds to the statement that at constant temperature, pressure varies inversely with volume.

Step 2: Evaluation of Charles' law
Charles' law states that for a fixed mass of gas maintained at constant pressure, the volume of the gas is directly proportional to its absolute temperature (\(V \propto T\)). Therefore, Charles' law corresponds to the statement that at constant pressure, volume is directly proportional to absolute temperature.

Step 3: Evaluation of Gay Lussac's law
Gay Lussac's law of combining volumes states that when gases react together to produce other gaseous products, the volumes of reactants and products bear a simple integer ratio to one another, provided temperature and pressure remain constant. Therefore, Gay Lussac's law corresponds to the statement regarding chemically reacting volumes being in the ratios of small integers.

Step 4: Evaluation of Avogadro's law
Avogadro's hypothesis establishes that equal volumes of all ideal gases under identical conditions of temperature and pressure contain equal numbers of molecules. Therefore, Avogadro's law corresponds to the statement that equal volumes of gases at identical temperature and pressure contain equal numbers of molecules.

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Pairing each gas law with its defining physical relationship yields: Boyle's law pairs with (III), Charles' law pairs with (I), Gay Lussac's law pairs with (II), and Avogadro's law pairs with (IV). Thus, the correct sequence of pairings is (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(II), (D)-(IV).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_KINETIC_THEORY_MATCHING_Q02 - Mathematical expressions for microscopic ideal gas parameters

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Physical Quantity) List-II (Formula / Expression)
(A) Pressure exerted by an ideal gas (I) \(\frac{3}{2} k_B T\)
(B) Root-mean-square molecular speed (II) \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2} n \pi d^2}\)
(C) Average translational kinetic energy per molecule (III) \(\sqrt{\frac{3 k_B T}{m}}\)
(D) Mean free path of molecules (IV) \(\frac{1}{3} \rho \overline{v^2}\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of pressure exerted by an ideal gas
From the kinetic theory of gases, the pressure \(P\) exerted by gas molecules colliding elastically with the container walls is given by: \[P = \frac{1}{3} n m \overline{v^2} = \frac{1}{3} \rho \overline{v^2}\] where \(n\) is number density, \(m\) is molecular mass, \(\rho = n m\) is mass density, and \(\overline{v^2}\) is mean-square speed. Therefore, pressure exerted by an ideal gas corresponds to \(\frac{1}{3} \rho \overline{v^2}\).

Step 2: Evaluation of root-mean-square molecular speed
The root-mean-square speed \(v_{\mathrm{rms}}\) is defined as the square root of the mean of squared speeds. Equating the average kinetic energy \(\frac{1}{2} m \overline{v^2}\) to \(\frac{3}{2} k_B T\) yields: \[v_{\mathrm{rms}} = \sqrt{\overline{v^2}} = \sqrt{\frac{3 k_B T}{m}}\] Therefore, root-mean-square molecular speed corresponds to \(\sqrt{\frac{3 k_B T}{m}}\).

Step 3: Evaluation of average translational kinetic energy per molecule
According to the kinetic interpretation of temperature, the mean translational kinetic energy per molecule depends solely on absolute temperature \(T\): \[E_{\mathrm{tr}} = \frac{1}{2} m \overline{v^2} = \frac{3}{2} k_B T\] Therefore, average translational kinetic energy per molecule corresponds to \(\frac{3}{2} k_B T\).

Step 4: Evaluation of mean free path of molecules
The mean free path \(l\) represents the average distance traveled by a molecule between successive collisions. Taking into account the relative velocity of all moving molecules of diameter \(d\) and number density \(n\): \[l = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2} n \pi d^2}\] Therefore, mean free path of molecules corresponds to \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2} n \pi d^2}\).

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Pairing each physical quantity with its exact kinetic formula yields: pressure corresponds to (IV), root-mean-square speed corresponds to (III), average translational kinetic energy corresponds to (I), and mean free path corresponds to (II). Thus, the correct sequence of pairings is (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(I), (D)-(II).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_KINETIC_THEORY_MATCHING_Q03 - Molar heat capacities of various molecular gas models

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Gas Model) List-II (Molar Heat Capacity at Constant Volume, \(C_V\))
(A) Monatomic ideal gas (I) \(\frac{7}{2} R\)
(B) Rigid diatomic ideal gas (II) \((3 + f) R\)
(C) Non-rigid diatomic gas with one vibrational mode (III) \(\frac{3}{2} R\)
(D) Polyatomic gas with \(f\) vibrational modes (IV) \(\frac{5}{2} R\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of monatomic ideal gas
A monatomic gas molecule possesses only \(3\) translational degrees of freedom. By the equipartition theorem, its internal energy per mole is: \[U = 3 \times \frac{1}{2} R T = \frac{3}{2} R T\] Differentiating with respect to temperature gives: \[C_V = \frac{dU}{dT} = \frac{3}{2} R\] Therefore, monatomic ideal gas corresponds to \(\frac{3}{2} R\).

Step 2: Evaluation of rigid diatomic ideal gas
A rigid diatomic molecule possesses \(3\) translational and \(2\) rotational degrees of freedom, totaling \(5\) degrees of freedom. Its internal energy per mole is: \[U = 5 \times \frac{1}{2} R T = \frac{5}{2} R T\] Differentiating with respect to temperature gives: \[C_V = \frac{dU}{dT} = \frac{5}{2} R\] Therefore, rigid diatomic ideal gas corresponds to \(\frac{5}{2} R\).

Step 3: Evaluation of non-rigid diatomic gas with one vibrational mode
A non-rigid diatomic molecule possesses \(3\) translational degrees of freedom, \(2\) rotational degrees of freedom, and \(1\) vibrational mode. Each vibrational mode contributes both kinetic and potential energy quadratic terms, providing \(2 \times \frac{1}{2} R T = R T\) per mole. The total internal energy per mole is: \[U = \frac{5}{2} R T + R T = \frac{7}{2} R T\] Differentiating with respect to temperature gives: \[C_V = \frac{dU}{dT} = \frac{7}{2} R\] Therefore, non-rigid diatomic gas with one vibrational mode corresponds to \(\frac{7}{2} R\).

Step 4: Evaluation of polyatomic gas with vibrational modes
A general non-linear polyatomic gas has \(3\) translational and \(3\) rotational degrees of freedom, along with \(f\) vibrational modes. Its internal energy per mole is: \[U = \left(3 \times \frac{1}{2} R T\right) + \left(3 \times \frac{1}{2} R T\right) + f R T = (3 + f) R T\] Differentiating with respect to temperature gives: \[C_V = \frac{dU}{dT} = (3 + f) R\] Therefore, polyatomic gas with \(f\) vibrational modes corresponds to \((3 + f) R\).

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Pairing each gas model with its respective molar heat capacity at constant volume yields: monatomic gas corresponds to (III), rigid diatomic gas corresponds to (IV), non-rigid diatomic gas corresponds to (I), and polyatomic gas corresponds to (II). Thus, the correct sequence of pairings is (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_KINETIC_THEORY_MATCHING_Q04 - Thermodynamic dependencies of molecular mean free path

questiontext.text:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Process / Molecular Property) List-II (Proportionality Dependence)
(A) Mean free path at constant pressure with respect to \(T\) (I) \(\propto T^0\) (independent of \(T\))
(B) Mean free path at constant volume with respect to \(T\) (II) \(\propto P^{-1}\) (inversely proportional to \(P\))
(C) Collision frequency at constant volume with respect to \(T\) (III) \(\propto T\) (directly proportional to \(T\))
(D) Mean free path at constant temperature with respect to \(P\) (IV) \(\propto T^{1/2}\) (directly proportional to \(\sqrt{T}\))

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of mean free path at constant pressure
The mean free path of a gas molecule is given by: \[l = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2} n \pi d^2}\] Using the ideal gas relation for number density \(n = \frac{P}{k_B T}\), the expression becomes: \[l = \frac{k_B T}{\sqrt{2} \pi d^2 P}\] At constant pressure \(P\), the mean free path is directly proportional to absolute temperature: \[l \propto T\] Therefore, mean free path at constant pressure with respect to \(T\) corresponds to \(\propto T\).

Step 2: Evaluation of mean free path at constant volume
For a fixed mass of gas of \(N\) molecules enclosed in a rigid container of constant volume \(V\), the number density \(n = \frac{N}{V}\) is constant. Since the molecular diameter \(d\) is invariant, the mean free path \(l = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2} n \pi d^2}\) remains strictly unchanged regardless of changes in temperature. Hence, \(l\) is independent of \(T\), behaving as \(\propto T^0\). Therefore, mean free path at constant volume with respect to \(T\) corresponds to \(\propto T^0\).

Step 3: Evaluation of collision frequency at constant volume
The collision frequency \(f_{\mathrm{coll}}\) of a gas molecule is the reciprocal of the mean free time: \[f_{\mathrm{coll}} = \frac{1}{\tau} = \sqrt{2} n \pi d^2 \langle v \rangle\] The average molecular speed \(\langle v \rangle = \sqrt{\frac{8 k_B T}{\pi m}}\) is directly proportional to \(\sqrt{T}\). Since number density \(n\) is constant at fixed volume: \[f_{\mathrm{coll}} \propto \langle v \rangle \propto T^{1/2}\] Therefore, collision frequency at constant volume with respect to \(T\) corresponds to \(\propto T^{1/2}\).

Step 4: Evaluation of mean free path at constant temperature
From the formula \(l = \frac{k_B T}{\sqrt{2} \pi d^2 P}\), when absolute temperature \(T\) is held constant, the product in the numerator is constant. Consequently, the mean free path varies inversely with pressure: \[l \propto \frac{1}{P} = P^{-1}\] Therefore, mean free path at constant temperature with respect to \(P\) corresponds to \(\propto P^{-1}\).

Step 5: Final Conclusion
Pairing each thermodynamic dependence with its proportionality relation yields: mean free path at constant pressure corresponds to (III), mean free path at constant volume corresponds to (I), collision frequency at constant volume corresponds to (IV), and mean free path at constant temperature corresponds to (II). Thus, the correct sequence of pairings is (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(II).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_KINETIC_THEORY_MCQ_Q01 - Molecular volume ratio in water vapour

questiontext.text: The density of liquid water is \(1000\text{ kg/m}^3\) and the density of water vapour at \(100^{\circ}\text{C}\) and \(1\text{ atm}\) is \(0.6\text{ kg/m}^3\). What is the ratio of the molecular volume to the total volume occupied by the water vapour under these conditions?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Density of bulk liquid water, \(\rho_{\text{liquid}} = 1000\text{ kg/m}^3\).
Density of water vapour, \(\rho_{\text{vapour}} = 0.6\text{ kg/m}^3\).
Temperature \(T = 100^{\circ}\text{C}\), Pressure \(P = 1\text{ atm}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Assume the molecules are closely packed in the liquid state such that the volume of the liquid state roughly represents the actual molecular volume of the molecules, with no change in mass during vaporization.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
For a given fixed mass \(M\) of water:
\[ V_{\text{liquid}} = \frac{M}{\rho_{\text{liquid}}}, \quad V_{\text{vapour}} = \frac{M}{\rho_{\text{vapour}}} \]
The fraction of molecular volume to the total vapour volume is:
\[ f = \frac{V_{\text{liquid}}}{V_{\text{vapour}}} = \frac{\rho_{\text{vapour}}}{\rho_{\text{liquid}}} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the numerical values into the ratio:
\[ f = \frac{0.6\text{ kg/m}^3}{1000\text{ kg/m}^3} = 6.0 \times 10^{-4} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The ratio is dimensionless, and since a gas is mostly empty space, a value much smaller than unity (\(6.0 \times 10^{-4}\)) is physically sound.
The final answer is \(6.0 \times 10^{-4}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_KINETIC_THEORY_MCQ_Q02 - Moles of gas in given volume

questiontext.text: A rigid container holds \(44.8\text{ litres}\) of an ideal gas at standard temperature and pressure (STP). How many moles of the gas are present in the container?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Volume of the gas, \(V = 44.8\text{ litres} = 44.8 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m}^3\).
Condition: Standard Temperature and Pressure (STP).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Standard molar volume of any ideal gas at STP is \(22.4\text{ litres/mol}\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The number of moles \(\mu\) is given by:
\[ \mu = \frac{V}{V_{\text{molar}}} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the given values:
\[ \mu = \frac{44.8\text{ L}}{22.4\text{ L/mol}} = 2.0\text{ mol} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Units evaluate to moles directly: \(44.8 / 22.4 = 2.0\).
The final answer is \(2.0\text{ mol}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_KINETIC_THEORY_MCQ_Q03 - Average kinetic energy of helium atom

questiontext.text: What is the average translational kinetic energy per molecule of helium gas at a temperature of \(27^{\circ}\text{C}\)? (Take Boltzmann constant \(k_{\mathrm{B}} = 1.38 \times 10^{-23}\text{ J/K}\)).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Temperature, \(t = 27^{\circ}\text{C}\).
Boltzmann constant, \(k_{\mathrm{B}} = 1.38 \times 10^{-23}\text{ J/K}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Helium behaves as an ideal monatomic gas in thermal equilibrium. Absolute temperature in kelvin is \(T = t + 273.15 \approx 300\text{ K}\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
From the kinetic interpretation of temperature, the average translational kinetic energy of a single molecule is:
\[ E = \frac{3}{2} k_{\mathrm{B}} T \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Convert temperature to kelvin:
\[ T = 27 + 273 = 300\text{ K} \]
Substitute values into the energy equation:
\[ E = \frac{3}{2} \times (1.38 \times 10^{-23}\text{ J/K}) \times 300\text{ K} = 1.5 \times 4.14 \times 10^{-21}\text{ J} = 6.21 \times 10^{-21}\text{ J} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The energy has dimensions of joules and magnitude of order \(10^{-21}\text{ J}\), consistent with molecular thermal energy at room temperature.
The final answer is \(6.21 \times 10^{-21}\text{ J}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_KINETIC_THEORY_MCQ_Q04 - Total translational energy of argon gas

questiontext.text: Calculate the total translational kinetic energy of \(2.0\text{ moles}\) of argon gas at a temperature of \(300\text{ K}\). (Universal gas constant \(R = 8.314\text{ J mol}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}\)).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Number of moles, \(\mu = 2.0\text{ mol}\).
Temperature, \(T = 300\text{ K}\).
Universal gas constant, \(R = 8.314\text{ J mol}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Argon is a noble, monatomic ideal gas having 3 translational degrees of freedom per molecule.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The total translational kinetic energy of \(\mu\) moles of an ideal gas is given by:
\[ E = \frac{3}{2} \mu R T \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the given numerical parameters:
\[ E = \frac{3}{2} \times 2.0\text{ mol} \times 8.314\text{ J mol}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1} \times 300\text{ K} \]
\[ E = 3.0 \times 8.314 \times 300 = 7482.6\text{ J} \approx 7.48 \times 10^3\text{ J} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking units: \(\text{mol} \times (\text{J}/(\text{mol}\cdot\text{K})) \times \text{K} = \text{J}\). The result \(7483\text{ J}\) is physically consistent.
The final answer is \(7.48 \times 10^3\text{ J}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_KINETIC_THEORY_MCQ_Q05 - Heat capacity ratio of rigid diatomic gas

questiontext.text: According to the law of equipartition of energy, what is the theoretical ratio of specific heat capacities \(\gamma = C_p / C_v\) for an ideal diatomic gas treated as a rigid rotator?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Gas type: Diatomic gas modeled as a rigid rotator (non-vibrating dumbbell shape).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
A rigid diatomic molecule has 3 translational degrees of freedom and 2 rotational degrees of freedom, giving a total of \(f = 5\) degrees of freedom.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
By the law of equipartition of energy:
\[ C_v = \frac{f}{2} R = \frac{5}{2} R \]
Using Mayer's relation \(C_p - C_v = R\):
\[ C_p = C_v + R = \frac{7}{2} R \]
The ratio of specific heat capacities is:
\[ \gamma = \frac{C_p}{C_v} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Compute the ratio:
\[ \gamma = \frac{\frac{7}{2} R}{\frac{5}{2} R} = \frac{7}{5} = 1.40 \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The ratio is greater than 1, dimensionless, and matches experimental values for \(\text{N}_2\) and \(\text{O}_2\) at room temperature.
The final answer is \(1.40\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_KINETIC_THEORY_MCQ_Q06 - Molar specific heat of monatomic gas

questiontext.text: What is the molar specific heat capacity at constant volume, \(C_v\), for an ideal monatomic gas in terms of the universal gas constant \(R\)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Gas classification: Ideal monatomic gas (such as He, Ne, or Ar).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
A point-mass monatomic gas possesses only 3 translational degrees of freedom and no rotational or vibrational modes.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The internal energy of one mole of a monatomic gas is:
\[ U = 3 \times \left(\frac{1}{2} k_{\mathrm{B}} T\right) N_{\mathrm{A}} = \frac{3}{2} R T \]
The molar specific heat at constant volume is defined by:
\[ C_v = \frac{\mathrm{d}U}{\mathrm{d}T} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Differentiate \(U\) with respect to \(T\):
\[ C_v = \frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}T}\left(\frac{3}{2} R T\right) = \frac{3}{2} R = 1.5 R \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Since \(C_p = C_v + R = \frac{5}{2} R\), this yields \(\gamma = 5/3 \approx 1.67\), which is established for monatomic gases.
The final answer is \(\frac{3}{2} R\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_KINETIC_THEORY_MCQ_Q07 - Dulong Petit specific heat of solids

questiontext.text: According to the law of equipartition of energy, what is the theoretical molar specific heat capacity of a monoatomic solid element at room temperature? (Take \(R = 8.314\text{ J mol}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}\)).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
System: Solid element of \(N_{\mathrm{A}}\) atoms per mole vibrating in 3 dimensions.
Universal gas constant: \(R = 8.314\text{ J mol}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Each atom behaves as a three-dimensional harmonic oscillator having 3 vibrational modes. Each vibrational mode contributes two quadratic energy terms (kinetic and potential energy), each with average energy \(\frac{1}{2} k_{\mathrm{B}} T\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Average energy per atom = \(3 \times (2 \times \frac{1}{2} k_{\mathrm{B}} T) = 3 k_{\mathrm{B}} T\).
Total internal energy per mole:
\[ U = 3 k_{\mathrm{B}} T \times N_{\mathrm{A}} = 3 R T \]
Molar heat capacity:
\[ C = \frac{\mathrm{d}U}{\mathrm{d}T} = 3 R \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the value of \(R\):
\[ C = 3 \times 8.314\text{ J mol}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1} = 24.94\text{ J mol}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1} \\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The calculated value matches experimental measurements for metals such as aluminium, copper, and silver (around \(24.5 - 25.5\text{ J mol}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}\)).
The final answer is \(24.94\text{ J mol}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_KINETIC_THEORY_MCQ_Q08 - Interatomic spacing in water vapour

questiontext.text: Given that liquid water has a density of \(1000\text{ kg/m}^3\) and water vapour at \(100^{\circ}\text{C}\) and \(1\text{ atm}\) has a density of \(0.6\text{ kg/m}^3\), estimate the average interatomic distance in water vapour if the interatomic separation in liquid water is approximately \(2.0\text{ \AA}\) and volume expands roughly by a factor of \(10^3\).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Density of liquid water \(\rho_l = 1000\text{ kg/m}^3\).
Density of water vapour \(\rho_v = 0.6\text{ kg/m}^3\).
Interatomic spacing in liquid water \(r_0 = 2.0\text{ \AA} = 2.0 \times 10^{-10}\text{ m}\).
Volume expansion factor \(\approx 10^3\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Following the textbook analysis (Example 12.3), when the available volume per molecule increases by a factor of \(10^3\), the linear dimensions scale as the cube root of the volume expansion factor.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Linear scaling factor:
\[ \text{Scale factor} = (V_{\text{ratio}})^{1/3} = (10^3)^{1/3} = 10 \]
Radius/boundary scale: \(r' = 10 \times 2.0\text{ \AA} = 20\text{ \AA}\).
The average distance between adjacent molecular centers is \(2 \times r'\).

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate the average distance:
\[ d_{\\text{avg}} = 2 \times (10 \times 2.0\text{ \AA}) = 2 \times 20\text{ \AA} = 40\text{ \AA} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The resulting distance of \(40\text{ \AA}\) (tens of angstroms) matches the standard textbook result for interatomic spacing in gases compared to solids/liquids (a few angstroms).
The final answer is \(40\text{ \AA}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_KINETIC_THEORY_MCQ_Q09 - Ratio of rms speeds of gases

questiontext.text: A flask contains argon and chlorine gas in thermal equilibrium at \(27^{\circ}\text{C}\). If the atomic mass of argon is \(39.9\text{ u}\) and the molecular mass of chlorine is \(70.9\text{ u}\), what is the ratio of the root mean square speed of argon atoms to that of chlorine molecules, \(v_{\mathrm{rms}}(\text{Ar}) / v_{\mathrm{rms}}(\text{Cl}_2)\)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Temperature of the mixture: \(T = 27^{\circ}\text{C} = 300\text{ K}\).
Molar mass of argon: \(M_{\text{Ar}} = 39.9\text{ g/mol}\).
Molar mass of chlorine: \(M_{\text{Cl}_2} = 70.9\text{ g/mol}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Both gases are in thermal equilibrium at the same temperature and obey ideal gas behaviour.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The root mean square speed of an ideal gas is given by:
\[ v_{\mathrm{rms}} = \\sqrt{\\frac{3RT}{M}} \\]
Since both gases are at identical temperature \(T\):
\[ \\frac{v_{\\mathrm{rms}}(\\text{Ar})}{v_{\\mathrm{rms}}(\\text{Cl}_2)} = \\sqrt{\\frac{M_{\\text{Cl}_2}}{M_{\\text{Ar}}}} \\]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the molecular masses into the ratio:
\[ \\frac{v_{\\mathrm{rms}}(\\text{Ar})}{v_{\\mathrm{rms}}(\\text{Cl}_2)} = \\sqrt{\\frac{70.9}{39.9}} = \\sqrt{1.7769} \\approx 1.33 \\]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Since argon is lighter than chlorine, argon molecules must have a higher rms speed (ratio > 1). \(1.33^2 \\approx 1.77\), confirming the calculation.
The final answer is \(1.33\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_KINETIC_THEORY_MCQ_Q10 - Temperature for equal root mean square speed

questiontext.text: At what absolute temperature is the root mean square speed of an atom in an argon gas sample equal to the root mean square speed of a helium gas atom at \(-20^{\circ}\text{C}\)? (Atomic mass of \(\text{Ar} = 39.9\text{ u}\), atomic mass of \(\text{He} = 4.0\text{ u}\)).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Temperature of helium, \(t_{\text{He}} = -20^{\circ}\text{C}\).
Atomic mass of helium, \(M_{\text{He}} = 4.0\text{ u}\).
Atomic mass of argon, \(M_{\text{Ar}} = 39.9\text{ u}\).
Condition: \(v_{\mathrm{rms}}(\text{Ar}) = v_{\mathrm{rms}}(\text{He})\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Both gases are treated as ideal monatomic gases. Temperature must be converted to the kelvin scale: \(T_{\text{He}} = -20 + 273 = 253\text{ K}\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The root mean square speed formula is:
\[ v_{\mathrm{rms}} = \sqrt{\frac{3RT}{M}} \]
Equating the rms speeds:
\[ \sqrt{\frac{3RT_{\text{Ar}}}{M_{\text{Ar}}}} = \sqrt{\frac{3RT_{\text{He}}}{M_{\text{He}}}} \implies \frac{T_{\text{Ar}}}{M_{\text{Ar}}} = \frac{T_{\text{He}}}{M_{\text{He}}} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Rearrange for \(T_{\text{Ar}}\):
\[ T_{\text{Ar}} = T_{\text{He}} \times \frac{M_{\text{Ar}}}{M_{\text{He}}} \]
Substitute the numerical values:
\[ T_{\text{Ar}} = 253\text{ K} \times \frac{39.9}{4.0} = 253 \times 9.975 = 2523.675\text{ K} \approx 2524\text{ K} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Since argon is approximately 10 times heavier than helium, it requires roughly 10 times higher absolute temperature to attain the same rms speed: \(253 \times 10 \approx 2530\text{ K}\).
The final answer is \(2524\text{ K}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_KINETIC_THEORY_MCQ_Q11 - Number of air molecules in a room

questiontext.text: Estimate the total number of air molecules in a room of capacity \(25.0\text{ m}^3\) at a temperature of \(27^{\circ}\text{C}\) and a pressure of \(1\text{ atm}\) (\(1.013 \times 10^5\text{ Pa}\)). (Take \(k_{\mathrm{B}} = 1.38 \times 10^{-23}\text{ J/K}\)).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Volume of the room, \(V = 25.0\text{ m}^3\).
Temperature, \(t = 27^{\circ}\text{C} \implies T = 300\text{ K}\).
Pressure, \(P = 1.013 \times 10^5\text{ Pa}\).
Boltzmann constant, \(k_{\mathrm{B}} = 1.38 \times 10^{-23}\text{ J/K}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Air is treated as an ideal gas mixture in macroscopic mechanical and thermal equilibrium.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The ideal gas law in terms of total molecule count \(N\) is:
\[ P V = N k_{\mathrm{B}} T \implies N = \frac{P V}{k_{\mathrm{B}} T} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the given values:
\[ N = \frac{(1.013 \times 10^5\text{ N/m}^2) \times (25.0\text{ m}^3)}{(1.38 \times 10^{-23}\text{ J/K}) \times 300\text{ K}} \]
\[ N = \frac{2.5325 \times 10^6}{4.14 \times 10^{-21}} = 0.6117 \times 10^{27} = 6.12 \times 10^{26}\text{ molecules} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking order of magnitude: \(25\text{ m}^3 = 25000\text{ L}\). Moles \(\approx 25000 / 22.4 \approx 1100\text{ mol}\). Molecules \(\approx 1100 \times 6 \times 10^{23} \approx 6.6 \times 10^{26}\), which closely agrees.
The final answer is \(6.12 \times 10^{26}\text{ molecules}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_KINETIC_THEORY_MCQ_Q12 - Growth of air bubble rising in lake

questiontext.text: An air bubble of volume \(1.0\text{ cm}^3\) rises from the bottom of a lake \(40\text{ m}\) deep where the temperature is \(12^{\circ}\text{C}\) to the surface where the temperature is \(35^{\circ}\text{C}\). If atmospheric pressure is \(1.013 \times 10^5\text{ Pa}\), density of water is \(1000\text{ kg/m}^3\), and \(g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2\), what is the volume of the bubble when it reaches the surface?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Initial volume at bottom: \(V_1 = 1.0\text{ cm}^3\).
Depth: \(h = 40\text{ m}\).
Temperature at bottom: \(T_1 = 12^{\circ}\text{C} = 285\text{ K}\).
Atmospheric pressure at surface: \(P_2 = P_0 = 1.013 \times 10^5\text{ Pa}\).
Temperature at surface: \(T_2 = 35^{\circ}\text{C} = 308\text{ K}\).
Density of water: \(\rho = 1000\text{ kg/m}^3\), \(g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Air inside the bubble obeys the ideal gas equation and does not dissolve into the water during its ascent.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Pressure at the bottom of the lake:
\[ P_1 = P_0 + \rho g h \]
By the combined ideal gas law:
\[ \frac{P_1 V_1}{T_1} = \frac{P_2 V_2}{T_2} \implies V_2 = V_1 \times \left(\frac{P_1}{P_2}\right) \times \left(\frac{T_2}{T_1}\right) \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate bottom pressure \(P_1\):
\[ P_1 = 1.013 \times 10^5 + (1000 \times 9.8 \times 40) = 1.013 \times 10^5 + 3.92 \times 10^5 = 4.933 \times 10^5\text{ Pa} \]
Calculate final volume \(V_2\):
\[ V_2 = 1.0\text{ cm}^3 \times \left(\frac{4.933 \times 10^5}{1.013 \times 10^5}\right) \times \left(\frac{308}{285}\right) \]
\[ V_2 = 1.0 \times 4.8697 \times 1.0807 = 5.263\text{ cm}^3 \approx 5.3\text{ cm}^3 \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The volume increases by roughly a factor of 5 because pressure drops by a factor of 4.9 while temperature increases slightly. This confirms physical plausibility.
The final answer is \(5.3\text{ cm}^3\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_KINETIC_THEORY_MCQ_Q13 - Percentage speed difference of uranium isotopes

questiontext.text: A gas sample of uranium hexafluoride contains two isotopic molecules: \(^{235}\text{UF}_6\) and \(^{238}\text{UF}_6\). Given that the atomic mass of fluorine is \(19\text{ u}\), what is the percentage difference in their average molecular speeds at any given temperature?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Isotope 1: \(^{235}\text{U}\) with atomic mass \(235\text{ u}\).
Isotope 2: \(^{238}\text{U}\) with atomic mass \(238\text{ u}\).
Fluorine atomic mass: \(19\text{ u}\).
Formula of gas: \(\text{UF}_6\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Both isotopic species are at the same temperature and behave as ideal gases in thermal equilibrium.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Molecular masses:
\[ M_1 = 235 + 6(19) = 235 + 114 = 349\text{ u} \]
\[ M_2 = 238 + 6(19) = 238 + 114 = 352\text{ u} \]
Average speed is inversely proportional to the square root of molecular mass:
\[ \frac{v_1}{v_2} = \sqrt{\frac{M_2}{M_1}} \]
Fractional difference is:
\[ \frac{\Delta v}{v_2} = \frac{v_1 - v_2}{v_2} = \sqrt{\frac{M_2}{M_1}} - 1 \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Calculate the ratio:
\[ \frac{v_1}{v_2} = \sqrt{\frac{352}{349}} = \left(1 + \frac{3}{349}\right)^{1/2} \approx 1 + \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{3}{349} = 1 + 0.0043 = 1.0043 \]
Convert to percentage:
\[ \frac{\Delta v}{v_2} \times 100\% \approx 0.43\% \approx 0.44\% \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
The lighter molecule moves faster by approximately \(0.44\%\), consistent with the standard Graham's law diffusion separation factor.
The final answer is \(0.44\%\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_KINETIC_THEORY_MCQ_Q14 - Heat required for heating helium gas

questiontext.text: A rigid cylinder of fixed volume \(44.8\text{ litres}\) contains helium gas at standard temperature and pressure (STP). How much heat is required to raise the temperature of the gas by \(15.0^{\circ}\text{C}\)? (Take \(R = 8.314\text{ J mol}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}\)).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Volume of container, \(V = 44.8\text{ L}\) (rigid, constant volume).
Initial conditions: Standard Temperature and Pressure (STP).
Temperature increment, \(\Delta T = 15.0^{\circ}\text{C} = 15.0\text{ K}\).
Gas constant, \(R = 8.314\text{ J mol}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Since volume is fixed, no work is done (\(W = 0\)), so by the First Law of Thermodynamics, \(Q = \Delta U = \mu C_v \Delta T\). Helium is an ideal monatomic gas.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Number of moles:
\[ \mu = \frac{V}{22.4\text{ L/mol}} = \frac{44.8}{22.4} = 2.0\text{ mol} \]
For a monatomic gas, molar specific heat at constant volume is:
\[ C_v = \frac{3}{2} R \]
Heat supplied at constant volume:
\[ Q = \mu C_v \Delta T \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the parameters:
\[ Q = 2.0\text{ mol} \times \left(\frac{3}{2} \times 8.314\text{ J mol}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}\right) \times 15.0\text{ K} \]
\[ Q = 3.0 \times 8.314 \times 15.0 = 45.0 \times 8.314 = 374.13\text{ J} \approx 374\text{ J} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking units: \(\text{mol} \times (\text{J}/(\text{mol}\cdot\text{K})) \times \text{K} = \text{J}\). The result \(374\text{ J}\) matches the textbook derivation exactly.
The final answer is \(374\text{ J}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_KINETIC_THEORY_MCQ_Q15 - Mean free path of nitrogen gas

questiontext.text: Estimate the mean free path of a nitrogen molecule in a cylinder containing nitrogen gas at a pressure of \(2.0\text{ atm}\) (\(2.026 \times 10^5\text{ Pa}\)) and a temperature of \(17^{\circ}\text{C}\). Take the molecular diameter to be \(2.0\text{ \AA}\) (\(2.0 \times 10^{-10}\text{ m}\)) and \(k_{\mathrm{B}} = 1.38 \times 10^{-23}\text{ J/K}\).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Pressure, \(P = 2.026 \times 10^5\text{ Pa}\).
Temperature, \(t = 17^{\circ}\text{C} \implies T = 17 + 273 = 290\text{ K}\).
Diameter of molecule, \(d = 2.0 \times 10^{-10}\text{ m}\).
Boltzmann constant, \(k_{\mathrm{B}} = 1.38 \times 10^{-23}\text{ J/K}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Nitrogen gas obeys the ideal gas equation. All molecules are in motion, requiring the \(\sqrt{2}\) factor in the mean free path formula.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Number density \(n\):
\[ n = \frac{P}{k_{\mathrm{B}} T} \]
Mean free path \(l\):
\[ l = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2} n \pi d^2} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
First compute \(n\):
\[ n = \frac{2.026 \times 10^5\text{ N/m}^2}{(1.38 \times 10^{-23}\text{ J/K}) \times 290\text{ K}} = \frac{2.026 \times 10^5}{4.002 \times 10^{-21}} = 5.062 \times 10^{25}\text{ m}^{-3} \]
Next compute \(l\):
\[ l = \frac{1}{1.414 \times (5.062 \times 10^{25}) \times \pi \times (2.0 \times 10^{-10})^2} \]
\[ l = \frac{1}{1.414 \times (5.062 \times 10^{25}) \times 3.1416 \times (4.0 \times 10^{-20})} \]
\[ l = \frac{1}{8.995 \times 10^6} = 1.11 \times 10^{-7}\text{ m} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
\(l \approx 1.11 \times 10^{-7}\text{ m} = 1110\text{ \AA} \approx 550 d\), which conforms to the expected mean free path order of hundreds to thousands of molecular diameters.
The final answer is \(1.11 \times 10^{-7}\text{ m}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_KINETIC_THEORY_MCQ_Q16 - Collision frequency of gas molecules

questiontext.text: For nitrogen molecules at \(17^{\circ}\text{C}\) with mean free path \(l = 1.11 \times 10^{-7}\text{ m}\) and average molecular speed \(\langle v \rangle = 468\text{ m/s}\), what is the collision frequency (rate of collisions per second experienced by a single molecule)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Mean free path: \(l = 1.11 imes 10^{-7} ext{ m}\).
Average molecular speed: \(\langle v angle = 468 ext{ m/s}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
The average time interval between two successive collisions for a molecule is \( au = l / \langle v angle\), and collision frequency is \( u = 1 / au\).

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The collision frequency \( u\) is given by:
\[ u = rac{\langle v angle}{l} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the numerical values:
\[ u = rac{468 ext{ m/s}}{1.11 imes 10^{-7} ext{ m}} = 4.22 imes 10^9 ext{ s}^{-1} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Units are \( ext{s}^{-1}\) (Hz), and a frequency of several billion collisions per second (\(\approx 4.2 imes 10^9 ext{ s}^{-1}\)) is typical for gas molecules at near atmospheric conditions.
The final answer is \(4.22 imes 10^9 ext{ s}^{-1}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_KINETIC_THEORY_MCQ_Q17 - Ratio of gas mass densities in mixture

questiontext.text: A vessel contains a mixture of neon (monatomic, atomic mass \(20.2\text{ u}\)) and oxygen (diatomic, molecular mass \(32.0\text{ u}\)). If the ratio of their partial pressures \(P_{\text{Ne}} : P_{\text{O}_2}\) is \(3 : 2\), what is the ratio of the mass density of neon to oxygen, \(\rho_{\text{Ne}} / \rho_{\text{O}_2}\)?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Ratio of partial pressures: \(P_1 / P_2 = 3 / 2 = 1.5\).
Molar mass of neon: \(M_1 = 20.2\text{ g/mol}\).
Molar mass of oxygen: \(M_2 = 32.0\text{ g/mol}\).
Both gases occupy the same volume \(V\) at temperature \(T\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Both gases behave as ideal non-reacting gases satisfying the ideal gas equation.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
From the ideal gas equation in terms of density:
\[ P = \frac{\rho R T}{M} \implies \rho = \frac{P M}{R T} \]
Since \(R\) and \(T\) are common to both gases:
\[ \frac{\rho_1}{\rho_2} = \left(\frac{P_1}{P_2}\right) \times \left(\frac{M_1}{M_2}\right) \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the given values:
\[ \frac{\rho_{\text{Ne}}}{\rho_{\text{O}_2}} = \left(\frac{3}{2}\right) \times \left(\frac{20.2}{32.0}\right) = 1.5 \times 0.63125 = 0.947 \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Even though neon has higher partial pressure (factor of 1.5), its lighter molar mass (factor of 0.63) compensates, giving a density ratio slightly less than 1 (0.947).
The final answer is \(0.947\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_KINETIC_THEORY_MCQ_Q18 - Root mean square speed of nitrogen

questiontext.text: Calculate the root mean square speed of a nitrogen molecule (\(\text{N}_2\)) at a temperature of \(300\text{ K}\). (Take \(R = 8.314\text{ J mol}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}\) and molar mass of \(\text{N}_2 = 28.0\text{ g/mol}\)).

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Absolute temperature, \(T = 300\text{ K}\).
Molar mass of \(\text{N}_2\), \(M = 28.0\text{ g/mol} = 0.028\text{ kg/mol}\).
Universal gas constant, \(R = 8.314\text{ J mol}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Nitrogen is treated as an ideal gas in thermal equilibrium.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
The root mean square speed is given by:
\[ v_{\mathrm{rms}} = \sqrt{\frac{3RT}{M}} \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Substitute the values with SI units:
\[ v_{\mathrm{rms}} = \sqrt{\frac{3 \times 8.314\text{ J mol}^{-1}\text{K}^{-1} \times 300\text{ K}}{0.028\text{ kg/mol}}} \]
\[ v_{\mathrm{rms}} = \sqrt{\frac{7482.6}{0.028}} = \sqrt{267235.7\text{ m}^2/\text{s}^2} \approx 517\text{ m/s} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Checking units: \(\sqrt{\text{J}/\text{kg}} = \sqrt{\text{kg}\cdot\text{m}^2\cdot\text{s}^{-2}/\text{kg}} = \text{m/s}\). A speed of \(517\text{ m/s}\) is consistent with the speed of sound and textbook values.
The final answer is \(517\text{ m/s}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_KINETIC_THEORY_MCQ_Q19 - Pressure exerted by gas molecules in vessel

questiontext.text: A vessel of volume \(2.0\text{ litres}\) contains \(1.0 \times 10^{23}\) molecules of a gas, each of mass \(5.0 \times 10^{-26}\text{ kg}\). If the root mean square speed of the molecules is \(600\text{ m/s}\), what is the pressure exerted by the gas on the walls of the vessel?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Number of molecules, \(N = 1.0 \times 10^{23}\).
Mass of each molecule, \(m = 5.0 \times 10^{-26}\text{ kg}\).
Volume, \(V = 2.0\text{ L} = 2.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m}^3\).
Root mean square speed, \(v_{\mathrm{rms}} = 600\text{ m/s}\).

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
Collisions of molecules with container walls are perfectly elastic, and the gas velocity distribution is isotropic.

Step 3: Relevant Formulae and Principles
Kinetic theory pressure formula:
\[ P = \frac{1}{3} n m \overline{v^2} = \frac{1}{3} \left(\frac{N}{V}\right) m v_{\mathrm{rms}}^2 \]

Step 4: Step-by-Step Working
Compute total mass of gas:
\[ M_{\text{total}} = N m = (1.0 \times 10^{23}) \times (5.0 \times 10^{-26}\text{ kg}) = 5.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ kg} \]
Compute mass density \(\rho\):
\[ \rho = \frac{M_{\text{total}}}{V} = \frac{5.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ kg}}{2.0 \times 10^{-3}\text{ m}^3} = 2.5\text{ kg/m}^3 \]
Calculate pressure:
\[ P = \frac{1}{3} \times 2.5\text{ kg/m}^3 \times (600\text{ m/s})^2 = \frac{1}{3} \times 2.5 \times 360000 = 300000\text{ Pa} = 3.0 \times 10^5\text{ Pa} \]

Step 5: Check and Final Answer
Units evaluate to \(\text{kg}/\text{m}^3 \times \text{m}^2/\text{s}^2 = \text{N}/\text{m}^2 = \text{Pa}\). The value of \(3.0 \times 10^5\text{ Pa}\) (\(\approx 3\text{ atm}\)) is reasonable.
The final answer is \(3.0 \times 10^5\text{ Pa}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_PHYSICS_KINETIC_THEORY_MCQ_Q20 - Heat capacity ratio with vibrational mode

questiontext.text: Consider a diatomic gas whose molecules possess, in addition to translation and rotation, one active vibrational mode. What is the ratio of specific heat capacities \(\gamma = C_p / C_v\) for this gas according to the equipartition theorem?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Given Data and Conditions
Gas: Diatomic gas with 1 active vibrational mode.

Step 2: Assumptions and Sign Conventions
